Fashion Review Analytics: From Raw Text to a Streamlit App

Women's Clothing Reviews (Kaggle)NLTK · scikit-learn · GensimHeuristic · VADER · MLStreamlit appTotal marks: 50

Project in Brief

Many product returns are announced in advance in the customer's own words. This project builds a small system that reads a fashion review and predicts whether the customer would recommend the product, so the quality team can look at risky products first. It cleans text with RegEx and NLTK, builds Bag-of-Words, TF-IDF, N-gram and Word2Vec features, compares four classifiers against a baseline, compares three NLP approaches, and deploys the best pipeline as a Streamlit app.

All 7 Steps

Step 1Completed

NLP Fundamentals, Preprocessing & RegEx

Explore the reviews, split the data, extract patterns and build the cleaning function.

  • 845 reviews with no text dropped; missing titles filled; full_text = Title + Review Text.
  • Always-"recommends" baseline: 0.819 accuracy. Trend has the highest not-recommended rate (25.4%). 187 reviews rate 4–5 stars but are still not recommended.
  • RegEx: size words (6,342 reviews), heights such as 5'4 (3,420 reviews), average ! count 0.42 (not recommended) vs 0.96 (recommended), so happy customers use more exclamation marks; no ALL-CAPS words were found because the review text is almost entirely lowercase; numbers to NUM, n't to not.
  • clean_text() in text_utils.py: lowercase, letters only, tokenise, stop-words (keeping not, no, nor), lemmatize.
Step 2Completed

Feature Extraction: BoW, TF-IDF & N-Grams

Turn text into numbers and see what each feature type captures.

  • Tiny 4-review corpus: BoW counts, TF-IDF weights (quality scores higher than dress because it is rarer) and the bigram "not worth" that carries Doc 4's meaning.
  • Real reviews, fitted on training data only: BoW and TF-IDF both 18,112 × 5,000, sparsity 99.46%; test matrix 4,529 × 5,000.
  • Highest average TF-IDF words: dress, not, love, top, fit, great, size, color, look, like.
Step 3Completed

Word Embeddings: Word2Vec (CBoW & Skip-gram)

Train word vectors on the training reviews and explore related words.

  • Both models: vocabulary 3,910 words, 100 dimensions, trained on training reviews only.
  • Similar words: small → large, big (CBoW) and large, xsmall (Skip-gram); cheap → flimsy, shiny; return → exchange, returned.
  • Pair similarity (Skip-gram): small–tight 0.51, large–loose 0.45, soft–comfortable 0.60, love–hate 0.41.
  • Skip-gram model saved as word2vec_skipgram.model.
Step 4Completed

Text Classification Pipeline

Build the baseline and four classifiers, then choose a decision threshold.

  • Models: A Bag-of-Words, B TF-IDF, C TF-IDF + N-grams, D averaged Skip-gram vectors.
  • Best pipeline: C (TF-IDF + N-grams), saved as recommend_pipeline.pkl and reloaded on 5 new reviews.
  • Top words pushing towards "not recommended": disappointed, not flattering, returning, unflattering, returned. Towards "recommends": love, perfect, great, comfortable, soft.

Step 5Completed

Different NLP Approaches & POS Tagging

Solve the same problem three ways on the first 1,000 test reviews, then mine complaint phrases.

ApproachNeeds training data?AccuracyRecall (0)F1 (0)
Heuristic (15 warning words, 1+ hit)No0.7830.3900.396
VADER (t = 0.4, tuned on 1,000 train reviews)No0.8400.3240.424
ML (TF-IDF + N-grams + LR)Yes0.8900.8790.744
  • POS tagging on 1,000 not-recommended reviews: most frequent adjective + noun phrases are poor quality (23), much fabric (20), usual size (16), high hopes (13) and good quality (12).
  • The quality team should check fabric, quality and sizing first, starting with the Trend department.
Step 6Completed

Streamlit App

A separate app.py loads recommend_pipeline.pkl and uses clean_text from text_utils.py.

  • Title and review inputs, Analyse button, recommend / NOT recommend message, probability metric and progress bar.
  • "Send to quality team" warning when the probability of not recommending is above 0.5.
  • RegEx statistics (words, exclamation marks, ALL-CAPS words), sidebar examples, threshold slider and POS-phrase expander.
  • Empty input shows Please enter a review. Tested with a positive, a negative, a mixed and an empty input.

Which Approach for Which Job?

Takeaway. Use a heuristic for a quick first version with no data, VADER for a fast general sentiment signal, and a trained ML pipeline when labelled data exists and quality matters. Here TF-IDF with bigrams caught 88% of unhappy customers, against 39% for the keyword rule and 32% for VADER.

Heuristic

Very easy to explain, but ignores context and needs a hand-made word list.

VADER

Ready in minutes, but measures general sentiment, not our recommend label.

TF-IDF + N-grams

Learns from labelled reviews and keeps small negations like "not worth".

Limitations: the data is from an international store, not an Indian platform; Hinglish reviews such as "kapda bahut cheap hai" would mostly fall outside the vocabulary; the model uses text only (no Rating or Department).
